intent: Create a distinctive, high-craft landing page for Du Bonheur that turns its real pâtisserie pedigree, sensory product experience, and Berlin identity into a modern digital experience
businessTruths: Du Bonheur is a real French pâtisserie in Berlin Mitte.
The site must represent real products and the real physical business truthfully.
The digital experience should make visiting, understanding the offer, and reaching the shop easy.
antiPrinciples: Do not default to generic beige luxury.
Do not use decorative Paris clichés.
Do not fabricate signature products as documentary imagery.
Do not add motion merely to signal premium quality.

creativeThesisCandidate.governingIdea: Treat French pastry craft as a sequence of precise transformations whose evidence remains visible, while Berlin restraint prevents the experience from becoming nostalgic or ornamental.
creativeThesisCandidate.whyThisProject: Du Bonheur can own the contrast between highly worked pastry craft and a contemporary Berlin context because both are grounded in the real shop and product experience.
principles: Reveal craft through transformation and evidence rather than decorative French symbolism.
Let product texture create sensory intensity while the surrounding interface stays restrained.
Use Berlin directness to sharpen rather than neutralize the pleasure of the pâtisserie.
Every medium should interpret transformation differently instead of repeating one pastry motif.
creativeThesisCandidate.selectionRationale: The idea joins the documented craft, sensory and Berlin truths into one behavior that can govern several different worlds without naming an implementation technology.

creativeWorldCandidates.label: Laminated Craft
creativeWorldCandidates.worldIdea: The experience behaves like a pastry being built and revealed in precise layers: dense sensory evidence appears through controlled cuts, overlaps and releases inside a disciplined editorial field.
creativeWorldCandidates.interpretationOfThesis: Transformation is made visible as layering and reveal, while the surrounding structure remains restrained enough to keep the experience contemporary rather than nostalgic.
creativeWorldCandidates.narrativeModel: progressive reveal from raw craft evidence to finished product and visit action
creativeWorldCandidates.compositionModel: asymmetric editorial planes with deliberate crops, overlaps and cut-like transitions between dense and quiet zones

typographyIntent.statement: Display typography should feel sharply edited and compressed against calm, highly legible body text; hierarchy comes from contrast in scale, measure and rhythm rather than decorative French styling.

creativeWorldCandidates.imageLanguage: extreme truthful macro crops of real pastry structure alternating with contextual shop evidence; product texture carries the sensory drama
creativeWorldCandidates.materialLanguage: paper, flour, glaze, laminated layers and metal work surfaces translated into restrained surface contrast rather than literal skeuomorphism
creativeWorldCandidates.motionLanguage: movement exposes layers, seams and before-after states with measured consequence; nothing floats decoratively
creativeWorldCandidates.interactionModel: users reveal craft evidence through controlled sectional disclosure and compare process-to-product relationships
creativeWorldCandidates.responsiveStrategy: mobile turns overlaps into ordered layer reveals while preserving crop tension, sensory scale shifts and clear visit/shop actions
creativeWorldCandidates.soundPolicy: Default to silence; subtle material sound is permitted only if it strengthens a specific transformation moment.

creativeWorldCandidates.label: Counter Ritual
creativeWorldCandidates.worldIdea: The site behaves like an intimate service ritual at the pâtisserie counter: arrival, attention, choice, preparation, handoff and return create the experience rhythm.
creativeWorldCandidates.interpretationOfThesis: Transformation becomes human sequence rather than visual layering, and Berlin restraint appears through direct service cues, uncluttered choices and practical clarity.
creativeWorldCandidates.narrativeModel: service sequence moving from arrival and appetite through choosing, preparation, handoff and visiting
creativeWorldCandidates.compositionModel: horizontal and vertical service zones organized like a working counter, with objects and copy positioned by task rather than editorial collage

typographyIntent.statement: Typography should feel conversational but exact: a warm display voice for appetite and a highly functional supporting voice for ordering, timing, location and product detail.

creativeWorldCandidates.imageLanguage: truthful human-scale product and shop photography framed as moments of service, handling, selection and handoff rather than isolated beauty shots
creativeWorldCandidates.materialLanguage: counter surfaces, wrapping, trays, hands and service objects create grounded tactility with minimal ornamental texture
creativeWorldCandidates.motionLanguage: short handoff-like movements, arrivals and state changes create rhythm; motion behaves like service rather than spectacle
creativeWorldCandidates.interactionModel: users make clear choices and receive immediate contextual response, with product, opening, route and shop information treated as service actions
creativeWorldCandidates.responsiveStrategy: mobile becomes the primary counter ritual: thumb-friendly choices, location/opening priority, immediate product context and short state transitions
creativeWorldCandidates.soundPolicy: Silence by default; ambient shop sound is allowed only as an optional contextual layer and never required for comprehension.
antiPatterns: long cinematic intro before useful information

creativeWorldCandidates.label: Berlin Proof Sheet
creativeWorldCandidates.worldIdea: The experience presents pastry craft as evidence: real products, process fragments, shop traces and precise notes are assembled like a contemporary proof sheet where sensory richness interrupts a disciplined Berlin record.
creativeWorldCandidates.interpretationOfThesis: Transformation is proven through accumulated evidence instead of staged luxury; restraint comes from documentary organization and direct language while macro sensory moments break the grid deliberately.
creativeWorldCandidates.narrativeModel: nonlinear evidence field that accumulates credibility before resolving into product, place and action
creativeWorldCandidates.compositionModel: strict modular evidence grid interrupted by occasional full-bleed sensory breaks and annotated details

typographyIntent.statement: Typography should behave like an authored publication system: one character-bearing editorial role, one neutral reading role and no automatic technical third voice; captions and annotations remain precise without becoming laboratory graphics.
antiPatterns: generic magazine serif plus grotesk pairing

creativeWorldCandidates.imageLanguage: real product, storefront, process and material evidence shown with documentary crops, contact-sheet groupings and occasional extreme sensory enlargement
creativeWorldCandidates.materialLanguage: proof marks, paper edges, production notes and raw surfaces appear sparingly as evidence cues rather than nostalgic craft decoration
creativeWorldCandidates.motionLanguage: evidence assembles, aligns, annotates and occasionally breaks scale; transitions clarify relationships rather than simulate physical pastry
creativeWorldCandidates.interactionModel: users scan, open, compare and connect evidence fragments, moving between overview and detail instead of following a single linear reveal
creativeWorldCandidates.responsiveStrategy: mobile converts the proof field into a deliberate evidence stack with preserved annotation relationships, selective sensory interruptions and no loss of essential business actions
creativeWorldCandidates.soundPolicy: No sound by default; this world should remain convincing as a quiet documentary object.

opportunityGaps: make pastry texture and process tactile online
combine French craft with Berlin restraint
use real-product editorial cropping instead of category clichés
unresolvedUnknowns: which existing product photos are licensed/high-resolution
whether online shop conversion or in-store visits are the primary commercial goal
